base_member_text: [L359-L366] (MED/grid-metric-indexing) Cross-advection of v uses s%dsu(...,1) throughout a two-dimensional loop and the first negative-flow gradient uses dsu(ie,1) for the i-to-ie interval, which is inconsistent with local curvilinear spacing.

[L751-L791, L802-L813] (MED/grid-metric-indexing) The continuity correction repeatedly fixes the unused metric coordinate at 1 (dsu(i,1), dnv(1,j), dsz(i,1), dnz(1,j)), despite the module claiming curvilinear support and looping over the full 2-D grid.
audit_member_text: [L360-L366, L760-L766, L785-L791, L806-L807, L922-L930] (HIGH/grid-metric/indexing) Multiple two-dimensional correction formulas hard-code the transverse metric index to 1 even though neighboring code uses the current i or j, making the scheme inconsistent on spatially varying curvilinear grids.

adversarial.rationale: The active advUV and huhv routines still use first-row/first-column metrics on a grid whose metrics can vary in both directions. The continuity-correction examples do not establish an additional runtime defect because its only call is commented out.

base_member_text: [L49-L80, L157-L160] (LOW/lifecycle-contract) Module work arrays are allocated once with the first grid shape and have no reinitialization or shape check, so repeated library initialization with a different grid would retain incompatible storage.
audit_member_text: [L26-L35, L49-L81, L157-L160, L481-L486, L744-L748] (LOW/lifecycle/state) Module-global work arrays are allocated only once and have no resize or teardown path, so reuse with a different grid shape leaves an incompatible saved allocation.

adversarial.rationale: The module initialization flags outlive the supplied spacepars instance, and the workspace allocations are neither shape-checked nor released. A later initialization with a different grid therefore retains the first allocation; no teardown caller resets these private workspaces.

base_member_text: [L784-L792] (HIGH/sign-inconsistency) The negative-v continuity correction lacks the leading minus used by the analogous negative-u branch, making the qy correction's sign inconsistent with the qx implementation.
audit_member_text: [L784-L792] (HIGH/numerical-sign) The negative-v qy continuity branch omits the sign reversal used by the corresponding negative-u branch and by the other second-order flux routines, yielding a correction with the opposite sign.

adversarial.rationale: The only call to flow_secondorder_con is commented out, and no other source caller exists. Its local boundary defect cannot affect the executed continuity update in this build.

base_member_text: [L622-L676] (HIGH/stale-work-array) The 1-D vertical-momentum path does not clear wrk1 globally and cycles inactive mask cells before zeroing them, so a flux left from an earlier call can enter an active neighbor's divergence.

[L291-L303, L378-L379, L612, L676] (MED/division-precondition) Second-order velocity corrections divide by hum, hvm, or hh without a local positive-depth guard at the update point; the broader stencil mindepth check does not protect every update path.

[L509, L552, L633] (LOW/mask-contract) Neighbor masks are multiplied and used as a real flux factor rather than reduced logically, so the code silently assumes mskZ values are strictly binary rather than merely zero/nonzero.

audit_member_text: [L751-L772, L774-L800, L802-L819] (HIGH/MPI-boundary) The continuity correction is computed with fixed whole-array loops and then unconditionally zeroes every local outer work-array edge without MPI-aware exchange or boundary tests, so subdomain-interface corrections can be discarded and the update can depend on decomposition.
dispositions.rationale: span-refuted: The local-edge truncations exist, but the only model call is commented out in flow_timestep.F90 L754-L758, with an explicit note that this continuity correction was removed. It therefore cannot cause the claimed decomposition-dependent update in the current model execution path.
